stand: Three years after Hamas's 7 October 2023 attack and a year into the Trump-brokered ceasefire, Gaza's war has not ended. Israeli forces control roughly two-thirds of the enclave and continue demolishing towns such as Rafah; OCHA says 1,431 Palestinians have been killed and 5,026 wounded since the ceasefire, on top of more than 74,245 killed overall. Hamas has not disarmed. Reconstruction, estimated at $71.4 billion, remains largely blocked; 94% of Gazans need shelter aid. Netanyahu vows no Hamas rule, with elections set for 27 October.

claims.text: Netanyahu vows there will be no Hamas rule in Gaza.
claims.by: Says: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu, at Mount Herzl memorial.

claims.text: Hamas has not disarmed one year into the ceasefire; Israel will not withdraw until it does.
claims.by: Says: Hamas agreed to hand weapons to a Palestinian technocratic government, rejects the word disarmament. Denies: Israel calls the plan unacceptable, insists on full disarmament first.

claims.text: OCHA counts 1,431 Palestinians killed and 5,026 wounded since the October 2025 ceasefire, revising the earlier rounded toll.
claims.by: Says: OCHA, citing Gaza Health Ministry figures.

claims.text: Israel says its post-ceasefire strikes target Hamas members trying to rearm and attack; Hamas denies this.
claims.by: Says: Israel. Denies: Hamas denies trying to rearm or attack.

claims.text: Israel's military says 170 people killed in Gaza who presented themselves as journalists were in fact militants; CPJ says the two lists mostly do not match and is still reviewing the evidence.
claims.by: Says: Israeli military (Brig Gen Effie Defrin). Disputes: CPJ (Jodie Ginsberg) says it will assess the evidence independently; ~78 names appear on both lists.

claims.text: CPJ says Israel's military is responsible for the vast majority of journalist deaths worldwide since 2023.
claims.by: Says: Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ).

claims.text: Aid agencies say Israel blocks essential shelter and reconstruction items as dual-use; Israel says it is meeting its obligations.
claims.by: Says: NRC and the Shelter Cluster say Israel blocks dual-use items. Denies: Israel/COGAT says about 600 trucks/day enter and it is meeting its obligations.

claims.text: Former FAO official Benjamin Davis says he was fired for highlighting hunger in Gaza; FAO says he breached staff conduct rules.
claims.by: Says: Benjamin Davis says fired over Gaza hunger work and weekly vigils. Denies: FAO cites breaches of the civil-servant conduct code; director-general Qu Dongyu says he fires staff for political games.

claims.text: Israeli Defence Minister Katz says there is no real solution for Gaza without Palestinian migration out of the territory.
claims.by: Says: Defence Minister Israel Katz. Denies: Israeli officials say there are no plans to remove the population by force; Trump backed away from the idea after international pushback.

claims.text: The US Treasury sanctioned a Hamas commander and two France-based individuals and charities for raising funds for Hamas, including via crypto.
claims.by: Says: US Treasury Department (Secretary Scott Bessent).

claims.text: None of the war goals Israel's government set after 7 October has been achieved, despite Hamas's reduced but intact fighting strength.
claims.by: Says: Israeli intelligence assessments cited by Al-Monitor; no official Israeli government confirmation of the fighter estimate.

claims.text: CPJ removed 19 names from its journalist-death list after its own investigations found them to be combatants, almost all overlapping with Israel's list of 170; it has excluded 27 combatants in total since the war began.
claims.by: Says: CPJ (Jodie Ginsberg).

claims.text: Benjamin Davis has filed a formal appeal against his FAO dismissal, seeking reinstatement and withdrawal of the accusations against him.
claims.by: Says: Benjamin Davis. Denies: FAO cites breaches of the civil-servant conduct code on impartiality and public comment on controversial matters.

claims.text: UN Secretary-General António Guterres calls for the Gaza ceasefire to become permanent and for humanitarian aid at scale.
claims.by: Says: UN Secretary-General António Guterres.

claims.text: The planned International Stabilization Force would deploy 20,000 troops and train 12,000 Palestinian police, with Indonesia, Morocco, Kazakhstan, Albania, Kosovo and Uganda committing personnel.
claims.by: Says: ISF commander US Major General Jasper Jeffers.

claims.text: Israeli politician Moshe Feiglin says Gaza's entire population, including babies and children, is "the enemy," and frames forced expulsion and annexation as a moral obligation.
claims.by: Says: Israeli politician Moshe Feiglin, to the Jerusalem Post.

claims.text: Acled says violence in Gaza fell 61% compared with the war's second year; 1,915 Palestinians were killed in Gaza and 165 in the West Bank over the past year, while Israel-Hezbollah fighting in Lebanon reached its highest level in the same period.
claims.by: Says: Acled analyst Nasser Khdour.

claims.text: A PCPSR poll finds support for Hamas has fallen to 24%, from 35% ten months earlier, while 72% of Palestinians still oppose disarming the group, fearing it would trigger a new war rather than Israeli withdrawal.
claims.by: Says: Palestinian Centre for Policy and Survey Research (PCPSR).

claims.text: Israel is using territorial control to pressure Hamas and Hezbollah into disarming, rather than withdrawing first.
claims.by: Says: Acled analyst Nasser Khdour.

claims.text: Access restrictions to 65% of Gaza remain an obstacle to reconstruction, since the remaining 35% is already overcrowded.
claims.by: Says: OCHA.

claims.text: The number of Gaza structures classed as completely destroyed grew 9% since the ceasefire was declared, as demolition has continued.
claims.by: Says: Unosat (UN satellite centre).

claims.text: Satellite imagery shows Israel's military has systematically razed Rafah, once home to a quarter of a million people, continuing demolitions since the ceasefire across the territory it still controls.
claims.by: Says: SCMP, based on satellite imagery analysis.

claims.text: 94% of Gaza's population urgently needs shelter and basic household aid, and 65% of families live in tents or improvised shelters.
claims.by: Says: OCHA.

claims.text: Israeli strikes destroyed or damaged 95.5% of Gaza's 815 education facilities by the end of 2025, leaving all school-age children without access; UN-backed learning spaces now enrol 565,000 children, with roughly 200,000 still excluded.
claims.by: Says: Unicef (facility damage); OCHA, September 2026 report (enrolment figures).

claims.text: More than 100,000 Gaza residents who fled during the war remain stuck abroad, unable to return.
claims.by: Says: Palestinian Authority data.

claims.text: Nine candidates with personal ties to the 7 October attack — bereaved relatives, former hostages' kin or combatants — are standing for rival parties in the 27 October election.
claims.by: Says: AFP analysis.

timeline.text: Israeli rescue operation in Nuseirat refugee camp kills 274 Palestinians and wounds 698, per Gaza's Health Ministry.
A strike near al-Awda Hospital in Nuseirat kills a man identified by his widow as her second husband.
Israeli military spokesman Effie Defrin announces 170 people posing as journalists in Gaza were militants.
Netanyahu vows there will be no Hamas rule in Gaza at the Oct 7 memorial ceremony.
US Treasury sanctions a Hamas commander and a France-based crypto fundraising network.
OCHA report counts at least 1,431 Palestinians killed and 5,026 wounded since the ceasefire took effect.
UN Secretary-General Guterres calls for the Gaza ceasefire to become permanent, ahead of the third anniversary of the 7 October attack.
Israeli military says four of its soldiers have been killed by Hamas actions since the ceasefire took effect.
Guardian reports Benjamin Davis has lodged a formal appeal against his FAO dismissal.
Hamas-led attack on Israel kills 1,221 people and 251 hostages are taken into Gaza.
Protesters gather outside Netanyahu's residence and the Knesset on the attack's third anniversary, demanding a state inquiry into the security failures of 7 October 2023.
Israeli strikes across Gaza kill at least four Palestinians, including a Civil Defence rescue worker near Kamal Adwan Hospital.
Ceasefire takes effect; remaining hostages released and hundreds of Palestinian prisoners freed.
A woman identifying as an Israeli diplomat photographs an FAO staff moment-of-silence vigil for Gaza dead and complains of harassment.
Israel is due to hold its first general election since the 7 October 2023 attack.
Israeli strikes on residential buildings in Gaza City kill about 308 members of one extended family.
An FAO seminar on hunger in Gaza draws a complaint from the Israeli mission to the FAO.
The National Committee for the Administration of Gaza is appointed, led by Ali Shaath.
IPC report finds Gaza aid trucks averaged 227/day since the ceasefire, under half the required minimum.
The Board of Peace unveils a $2.45 billion plan to begin rebuilding Gaza.
FAO director-general Qu Dongyu publicly threatens to fire more staff for what he calls political activism on human rights.
CPJ removes 19 names from its journalist-death list after concluding they were combatants, mostly overlapping with Israel's 170-name list.
UN, EU and World Bank assessment estimates Gaza's reconstruction needs at $71.4 billion over the next decade.
Unosat satellite assessment finds 82% of Gaza's structures damaged.
Benjamin Davis's FAO contract is not renewed; he leaves the Rome headquarters after 26 years.

headline: Israel keeps razing Gaza as war passes third anniversary
